manual_review.detail: Both outputs cover contract October 2006, July 2007 commencement, approximately 285 delayed IFC drawings, six-week programme delay, six-month notified delay, and Revision 8 target of 16 December 2009. Key claims checked against their cited excerpts. Neither fully explains the contractor/design responsibility distinction requested in the broad topic.

Coair includes a JRC transport-modelling contract award unrelated to the central MUDFA chronology. Both outputs repeat some contract/business-case material. Similar row totals do not prove unique or complete events.

manual_review.assessment: Completion is not reliable on the first attempt
manual_review.detail: First Coair run failed after built-in retries at OverviewModel validation: source_ids exceeds three and/or overview_claims exceeds five. One explicitly recorded fresh repeat completed without changing application code or prompts. First failure remains part of the result. The corresponding constraints are shared with RAG.

manual_review.assessment: Different coverage on the same input corpus
manual_review.detail: RAG produced four event rows; the completed Coair repeat produced nine. Both correctly describe selected construction dates as programmed rather than completed. RAG includes the 13 October earthworks finish; Coair includes 29 October HV supply quote expectations. Both include the 6 November depot access bridge drawings milestone. The DCR0010 prior-approval event in the older reference is absent. Coair repeats one culvert milestone and adds broad project/OLE/staff context; RAG includes a Baird Drive transmittal. More rows is not a quality score.

Both outputs explain PB/SDS utility-data assessment, diversion design and assistance to tie. Coair adds the dated PB extension-of-time claim and quantitative diversion findings; RAG additionally describes tram-slab-depth clashes. Selected source excerpts support the central responsibility narratives.

Coair entry 6.1.5 groups retrospective ground-investigation and approximately 59000m actually undertaken assertions under 4 December 2007. TRI00000111_C witness statement page 3 explicitly associates that date with design-programme documents, but does not independently date every subsequent assertion to that day. This is a temporal-support gap, not proof that the underlying quantities are false. A dated claim cover alone also does not establish actual submission on that date.

verdict.controlled_reviewed_pilot: reasonable after assigning and loading the intended corpus in the chosen environment
verdict.reason: Format-completion reliability, temporal support and topical coverage need strengthening; production corpus/library/hosting migration is not performed by this test.

limitations: Three case studies plus one explicit Coair Gogar repeat, not a statistical reliability sample.
Native runtime/source code in disposable stores; not seven public UI journeys.
A RAG Gogar 3GiB OOM probe is excluded from content comparison and separately recorded. Later runs explicitly cap DuckDB at 1GiB; timings are not matched performance benchmarks.
Master-event stores start empty in both clones; native audit discovery falls back to normal retrieval.
Automatic date regex checks found no mismatch in their narrow supported cases; manual review still found a temporal-attribution gap. No exhaustive factual/coverage sign-off.
Current staging API has 2GiB and three sample PDFs; full-corpus engine QA uses up to 3GiB. Full-data deployment capacity and original-file/library mapping remain gates.
